video-car-mechanics-101-1z6ol5x450g-yout.summary: In this interview-style overview from Backyard Barn Finds, Joe of JWC Performance walks through practical LS-swap considerations for a classic car. The discussion centers on budget-driven choices (e.g., Dart blocks as a cost-effective option), fitment challenges (engine mounts, crossmember, exhaust clearance), cooling and capacity (radiator and twin fans; Vintage Air front-runner kit vs factory setups), and modern electrical/wiring approaches (updated harnesses, SpearTech PCM integration). The video also covers fuel delivery strategies (in-tank pump and new tank), and EFI versus carbureted planning, with hands-on notes about billet valve covers and coil-pack mounting. The overall message emphasizes balancing cost, reliability, and drivability when converting a classic car to modern LS power with modern electronics.
video-car-mechanics-101-1z6ol5x450g-yout.title: How to LS Swap your CLASSIC CAR for Dummies!

video-car-mechanics-101-3ngbm6zrppo-yout.summary: This How a Car Works video explains engine valves by detailing the flow path through the intake and exhaust ports, the purpose of valves in opening and sealing that path, and the advantages of multi-valve configurations. It then dissects the valve assembly—stem, head, face, and seat—covering how a precise seal is achieved and why finish and material choices matter for heat dissipation. The presentation contrasts intake and exhaust valves, discusses port sizing and cross-sectional area, explains valve guides and seals, and outlines the role of the valve spring and the risk of valve float. It also introduces valve timing concepts, the difference between interference and non-interference engines, common valve faults (burnt and bent valves), and concludes with an installation note and a look ahead to camshaft work.
video-car-mechanics-101-3ngbm6zrppo-yout.title: Everything about Engine Valves

video-car-mechanics-101-75xv6muz-q4-yout.summary: This instructional video from 1A Auto explains spark plug fundamentals relevant to cars, trucks, SUVs, and vans. It covers differences in seating styles (beveled vs flat), shank length implications, and electrode geometry across copper, platinum, and iridium plugs. The presenter emphasizes following manufacturer specifications for plug type and gap, explains how heat range relates to the porcelain/ceramic exposed area, and highlights maintenance considerations such as service intervals and torque. Practical how-tos include selecting the correct gap with various tools, avoiding improper gapping on platinum or iridium tips, using dielectric grease for easier installation and moisture protection, and inspecting plugs for cracks or wear. The video also discusses tools (spark plug sockets with rubber grommets, gap gauges) and cautions against reusing worn gaskets or mis-seating plugs, all framed within a practical, hands-on demonstration on a workbench.
video-car-mechanics-101-75xv6muz-q4-yout.title: Learn All About Spark Plugs for Cars, Trucks, SUVs and Vans!

video-car-mechanics-101-7rjlf-05xzi-yout.summary: Len from 1A Auto uses a 2010 Nissan Altima as the reference example to explain a rear-end clunking noise heard over bumps. The video identifies two primary suspects in the suspension linkage: the sway bar bushing (rubber supports for the stabilizer bar) and the sway bar link (with a ball-and-socket joint). He explains that stretched or worn bushings allow the bar to move and create noise, and that a worn ball-and-socket in the link can produce a knocking sound when the vehicle encounters bumps. The guidance concludes with a practical replacement recommendation: if diagnosing these parts, replacement of both the sway bar bushings and the sway bar link is commonly done together, and the video suggests 1A Auto as a source for parts.
video-car-mechanics-101-7rjlf-05xzi-yout.title: Clunking Noise When Driving Your Car, SUV or Truck Over Bumps?

video-car-mechanics-101-byeddkxpnfy-yout.summary: The video from How a Car Works explains the role of the water pump in a typical automotive cooling system, using a Mazda MX-5 Miata as the exemplar. It covers coolant composition (roughly 50/50 water and ethylene glycol), the closed cooling loop path from radiator to engine and back, and the thermostat’s role in regulating flow. The pump is shown as belt-driven and mounted at the front of the engine, driving the coolant through the engine and to the radiator. The internals are explored—an impeller inside a volute, a shaft-driven bearing, and a mechanical seal with a Weep hole—along with common failure modes. The video contrasts belt-driven pumps with electric pumps, discusses heat soak after engine shutdown, and notes maintenance practices such as replacing the pump as a unit during timing belt service. Practical diagnostic cues and model examples (BMW, Audi, Prius/Lexus hybrids) are highlighted to illustrate the varying implementations in modern cars.
video-car-mechanics-101-byeddkxpnfy-yout.title: Water pumps: Explained in super detail

video-car-mechanics-101-eupaxwjaeg-youtu.summary: This video explains the engine block as the core structure that houses cylinders and supports accessories, detailing material choices (cast iron, aluminium alloys, and occasional billet blocks), manufacturing steps (casting vs. machining), cylinder preparation (liners, bonding/coatings, and honing), the critical flatness of the deck for a proper head gasket seal, the oil and cooling passages that service the engine, and essential assembly aspects (crankcase, main caps, sump, core plugs, engine mounts, and bosses). It also covers practical nuances such as the purpose of crosshatch honing, the difference between liners and coatings in aluminium blocks, the role of oil jets, and how coolant flow is designed to avoid air pockets and excessive piston wear. The narration blends theory with on-vehicle demonstration to connect block design to engine reliability and performance.
video-car-mechanics-101-eupaxwjaeg-youtu.title: Everything about Engine Blocks

video-car-mechanics-101-fpjowekzegi-yout.summary: The video provides a guided tour of the major systems and assemblies that constitute a car. It starts with an overview of the key subsystems—body-on-frame, engine, transmission, suspension with Wheel and tires, control systems, and electrical systems—then explains body-on-frame versus unibody construction, front-engine placement, the 4-stroke engine cycle and its subsystems, how the engine connects to the drive Wheel via the powertrain, and common drive layouts (front-, rear-, and all-wheel drive). The sections cover suspension components, wheel and tire features, steering and braking controls, engine and transmission controls, and the basics of automotive electrical systems, before inviting viewers to watch more videos. The content is presented with brief definitions and visual cues typical of a high-level introductory explain-and-see approach.
video-car-mechanics-101-fpjowekzegi-yout.title: Сar anatomy: The Basics / How cars work? (3D animation)

video-car-mechanics-101-khozfrn5br8-yout.summary: In this 1A Auto lesson, Mike demonstrates why you should not over-tighten an oil drain plug. He describes the drain plug as threading into a small insert in a sheet-metal oil pan and notes that a quarter-turn past snug is sufficient. The video then shows an attempt to over-tighten with excessive force, including warnings about using air tools or very long wrenches, which can strip the threads. As tightening continues, the plug stops tightening and begins to spin, indicating cross-threading. The plug becomes cross-threaded and stuck, illustrating a worst-case outcome that may require drilling out the plug or replacing the oil pan. The core takeaway is to tighten only to snug, then an additional quarter-turn, and to avoid overdoing it to prevent thread damage and potential costly pan replacement.
video-car-mechanics-101-khozfrn5br8-yout.title: Why You Should Never Over Tighten A Drain Plug!

video-car-mechanics-101-muh41rf-qdm-yout.summary: This tutorial-clip from 1A Auto demonstrates diagnosing a sticking door lock actuator on a 2014 Subaru Forester. The host first confirms that the lock on one door only moves a short distance and produces an audible cue, then systematically tests the mechanism by inspecting the cables and opening the door panel to access the lock actuator. He identifies binding in the locking cable, disassembles the actuator to inspect internal components, and demonstrates how the lock motor translates rotation into cable motion. The video concludes with a plan to replace the faulty unit and a note that viewers can watch 1A Auto’s replacement video for the actual part install.
video-car-mechanics-101-muh41rf-qdm-yout.title: Car Door Lock Not Working Right? How to Diagnose Door Lock Actuator

video-car-mechanics-101-nmhsk41oqzq-yout.summary: This 1A Auto tutorial demonstrates no-tool diagnostic techniques for common vehicle symptoms. The host emphasizes using known-good parts to test circuits and components, then isolating the fault through straightforward swaps, visual inspections, and level checks. Covered areas include electrical faults (bulbs, switches, relays, fuses, speakers, ignition components), engine roughness (wiring, vacuum lines, connectors), fluid levels (oil, transmission fluid, coolant), battery health, and basic suspension/tire diagnostics. The approach centers on confirming whether a fault lies in a component or in the surrounding wiring or system by substituting a similar-known-good part and observing results, with cautions about safe handling when the engine is running and when testing power systems.
video-car-mechanics-101-nmhsk41oqzq-yout.title: How to Diagnose Your Car, Truck, SUV - With No Special Tools!

video-car-mechanics-101-of8p8ekzqva-yout.summary: This trailer introduces a multi-hour educational series that promises a complete teardown and rebuild of a Mazda MX-5 Miata, explained piece by piece with a focus on on-car demonstrations and high-fidelity 3D graphics. The host outlines a learning approach that emphasizes understanding how each component functions in situ, alongside plans for interactive 3D models accessible on web and mobile, with eventual virtual reality integration. The video highlights key systems and parts to be covered (engine, transmission, ABS, MAF, radiator cap), the use of specific tools, and a hands-on philosophy that includes dealing with real-world issues like rust and seized bolts. A pre-order drive is presented to fund production and earn participant recognition in credits.
video-car-mechanics-101-of8p8ekzqva-yout.title: How a Car Works Trailer

video-car-mechanics-101-ol99t-iswi-youtu.summary: This video provides a practical overview of mass air flow (MAF) sensors commonly found in modern fuel-injected engines. It explains the sensor’s role in measuring air volume and density to help the engine computer balance air and fuel, outlines common symptoms of a failing or dirty sensor (including hard starts, reduced fuel economy, hesitation, and a check engine light with code P0101), and describes common failure modes such as intake leaks and dirty air filters. It also demonstrates basic diagnostics concepts (using basic tools or an OBD scanner), and presents a hands-on cleaning procedure using dedicated MAF cleaner, with cautions against improper cleaning techniques and irreversible damage. The video emphasizes safety, proper reassembly checks, and ECU reset steps after servicing the sensor.
video-car-mechanics-101-ol99t-iswi-youtu.title: What Does a Mass Air Flow Sensor Do in a Car, Truck, SUV?

video-car-mechanics-101-p0jhsf-zcrm-yout.summary: This tutorial explains the basic mechanics of a scissor jack, outlines safety precautions for roadside or drive-by use, demonstrates proper placement at the pinch-weld lift points, and contrasts scissor with other jack types (bottle and floor variants). The presenter emphasizes that scissor jacks are emergency use tools, shows how the threaded rod drives the two arms to lift the vehicle, and walks through setup steps (wheel chocks, parking brake, correct placement) and the reversal to lower, including cautions about quick tire changes and returning the jack to its stored location.
video-car-mechanics-101-p0jhsf-zcrm-yout.title: How to Use a Scissor Jack to Raise Your Car, Truck, or SUV

video-car-mechanics-101-p5ra9bmtylo-yout.summary: This short technical deep-dive explains why ferrous metals like steel rust, how water, oxygen, and electrolytes accelerate corrosion, and why different metals form distinct oxide barriers. It contrasts porous iron oxide (rust) with protective oxides like aluminium oxide, and covers practical protective strategies including paints and coatings, galvanizing (sacrificial zinc), and chrome plating. The host also notes real-world accelerants such as coastal salt and winter road salt, emphasizes maintenance implications for vehicle bodies and internal parts, and previews rust-removal techniques in a future episode.
video-car-mechanics-101-p5ra9bmtylo-yout.title: Rust and Corrosion: A 10 minute guide

video-car-mechanics-101-sapgx-1qc4m-yout.summary: In this instructional video, host EricTheCarGuy walks through the basic components and functions of a conventional internal combustion engine using a 1.8 liter Honda Integra engine as a visual reference. The talk covers terminology (engine vs. motor), major assemblies (valve train, camshafts, timing system, ignition, intake/exhaust manifolds), and critical subsystems (valves, springs, seals, pistons, rings, crankshaft, oiling system, and cooling-related components). The video emphasizes how timing and geometry affect engine breathing, torque, and horsepower, and it includes practical anecdotes about common designs (DOHC, distributor ignition, carbureted vs. fuel-injected layouts) and the trade-offs engineers balance in automotive design.
video-car-mechanics-101-sapgx-1qc4m-yout.title: Dissecting an Engine, The Basic Parts and Their Functions - EricTheCarGuy

video-car-mechanics-101-wjqo82p5264-yout.summary: This video provides a foundational overview of a typical hydraulic clutch system for passenger cars and light-duty trucks. It explains each major component—pedal, clutch master cylinder, hydraulic line, slave cylinder, clutch fork, release (throw-out) bearing, pressure plate, clutch disc, flywheel, and pilot bearing/bushing—and describes how hydraulic input from the pedal ultimately frees and engages the clutch via the release bearing pushing the pressure plate fingers against the clutch disc against the flywheel. The host then presents a kit of replacement parts, demonstrates expected assembly order, and discusses on-vehicle layout. A substantial portion of the video is devoted to diagnosing common clutch problems observed in shop practice, including pilot shaft bushing wear, disc wear patterns, worn springs, and a noisy/dragging throw-out bearing, along with signs of hydraulic leakage from the slave and master cylinders. Practical diagnostic checks include inspecting fluid level and condition, detecting leaks via a leaky slave or boot, confirming road-test engagement height to distinguish wear from misadjustment, and adjusting the clutch master to restore firm pedal feel. The video closes with maintenance guidance emphasizing gentle clutch use, regular inspection of hydraulic components, and the importance of replacing worn parts to preserve system health and safety.
video-car-mechanics-101-wjqo82p5264-yout.title: How a Clutch System Works & How to Diagnose Problems

video-car-mechanics-101-x70vqmrxrbs-yout.summary: This video provides a structured overview of an internal combustion engine, outlining the core components and their roles in converting fuel energy into mechanical work. It covers the cylinder block and head, crankcase and oil pan, lubrication and cooling passages, manifolds, gaskets, liners, pistons and rings, connecting rods, crankshaft, camshaft, flywheel, and the valve system, with explanations of flow types, lubrication paths, and timing mechanisms. The narration ties each part to its function in fuel combustion, power transmission, and engine efficiency.
video-car-mechanics-101-x70vqmrxrbs-yout.title: Car Engine Parts & Their Functions Explained in Details | The Engineers Post

video-car-mechanics-101-xcm9ufgpbf4-yout.summary: This 1A Auto guide provides a concise, step-by-step routine for preparing a car that has sat for weeks before returning to the road. It covers battery readiness with a digital charger, cautions about jump-starts, and follows with fluids verification and leak checks, washer fluid top-off, tire pressure and wiper inspection, removal of hood debris, and finally a careful engine start and short warm-up. The video also describes early brake feel after sitting (possible rust on rotors) and recommends a brief, gradual stop pattern to clear it. The overall goal is to help drivers head back on the road safely after a period of inactivity, rather than merely starting and driving away.
video-car-mechanics-101-xcm9ufgpbf4-yout.title: What to Check Before Driving If Your Car Has Been Sitting a While

video-car-mechanics-101-xg5ok4slpge-yout.summary: This 1A Auto guide on torque wrenches explains how to apply correct rotational force to automotive fasteners, with practical demonstrations of setting and reading torque values, choosing appropriate drive sizes, and following a proper tightening sequence. The video compares click-type and beam-type wrenches, discusses common errors (such as rapid clicking and using a torque wrench as a breaker bar), and covers maintenance and calibration to preserve accuracy. It also introduces torque-angle gauges for high-torque applications and outlines lug-pattern sequences for multi-lug Wheel.
video-car-mechanics-101-xg5ok4slpge-yout.title: How to Use a Torque Wrench Properly

video-car-mechanics-101-xluk0xdpcsy-yout.summary: The video from 1A Auto demonstrates inspecting two dry drive belts on a vehicle that uses manual tensioners (no auto tensioner). The presenter notes squealing on startup as belts wear, identifies wear indicators such as cracks, fraying, and stiffness, and compares worn belts to a new belt. He explains that automatic tensioners can mask wear, whereas manual tensioners allow wear to show as slipping and noise. The lesson concludes with replacing the belts and removing the squeal. The guidance emphasizes visual and tactile belt checks and replacing worn belts rather than attempting to retension them.
video-car-mechanics-101-xluk0xdpcsy-yout.title: How to Properly Inspect your Engine Belts

video-car-mechanics-101-xrcma-gao8-youtu.summary: This tutorial-style video demonstrates how warped brake rotors manifest during driving and braking. It demonstrates common symptoms—lurching in the seat, left-right wheel vibration, a pulsating brake pedal distinct from ABS activation—and uses a highway test and an off-ramp braking sequence on a 2005 Cadillac CTS to illustrate the phenomena. The presenters conclude that the observed symptoms indicate a need for front brake pad and rotor replacement to restore smooth, safe stopping, and they promote 1A Auto parts as a source for replacement components.
video-car-mechanics-101-xrcma-gao8-youtu.title: How to Diagnose Warped Rotors on your Car

video-car-mechanics-101-xv9wvovdqm0-yout.summary: This 1A Auto tutorial demonstrates two practical methods for assessing tire tread depth across multiple tires: using a digital tread depth gauge and performing a penny test. The host shows how to place a gauge on the tread to quantify remaining life, compares readings across different tires, and explains how to interpret results (including when replacement may be needed). The penny test is demonstrated as a quick visual check, with notes on how to read Lincoln’s head exposure to estimate depth. The video also highlights the importance of checking across the full tread, not just the outer edge, and describes wear patterns influenced by tire inflation and wheel alignment. Throughout, the presenters compare measurements (including values expressed in 32nds of an inch) to determine tire condition and potential safety implications.
video-car-mechanics-101-xv9wvovdqm0-yout.title: How to Check Your Tire Tread Depth with a Gauge or a Penny

video-car-mechanics-101-yeb7zft-79k-yout.summary: In this instructional overview, Len from 1A Auto guides viewers through fundamental under-the-hood checks and considerations. The video emphasizes using the owner's manual as a starting point, then details practical checks and observations across several systems: locating the hood release and safety concerns, brake master cylinder and fluid level with leak indicators, coolant/pressure-cap considerations in a sealed cooling system, and cooling fan types. It also covers the air intake path and mass airflow sensor visibility, power steering fluid levels, engine oil dipstick technique and oil grade, transmission fluid checks, washer fluid basics, battery condition and terminal health, engine computer/fuse box awareness, ignition components, alternator and serpentine belt condition, and AC condensation. Throughout, the host underscores safety (not opening hot caps) and maintenance habits (referencing the owner’s manual and a regular maintenance schedule).
video-car-mechanics-101-yeb7zft-79k-yout.title: Under the Hood Basics! Learn About the Stuff Under Your Car's Hood!

video-car-mechanics-101-ympr8-mkkew-yout.summary: In this tire-focused guide, Sue from 1A Auto explains how to read and interpret tire size codes, age, and proper maintenance to maximize safety and performance. The video covers decoding tire size (width, aspect ratio, radial construction, and rim diameter), understanding speed ratings, locating the official tire size on the door placard and the spare, and identifying tire age from the date code. It also demonstrates practical topics like tire pressure, using gauges, tread-depth checks (with gauges and the Lincoln penny method), and when to repair vs replace. The discussion extends to patching vs plugging, the importance of rotation, and the role of alignment for front-, rear-, and all-wheel-drive vehicles, including the need for four matching tires on AWD systems and seasonal considerations for snow tires. Practical buying guidance, maintenance cadence, and the rationale behind many recommendations are tied back to safety and performance considerations.
video-car-mechanics-101-ympr8-mkkew-yout.title: Everything You Need to Know About Tires on Your Car, Truck or SUV

video-car-mechanics-101-yzuf1ytsxdm-yout.summary: In this instructional clip from 1A Auto, the presenter guides viewers through a thorough frame-condition check before lifting or working under a vehicle. The video emphasizes that most repairs require raising and supporting a vehicle, and demonstrates a step-by-step assessment: starting with a visual inspection to identify surface rust and structural loss, then probing for softness with a hammer to reveal weak metal and missing sections, and finally highlighting more severe findings such as cracked/stressed welds, detached transmission brackets, and severely rotted frame sections. The instructor stresses that even if some areas look solid, other sections can be dangerously compromised, and concludes that the truck in the video is not safe to drive, jack up, or work under. The tone reinforces safety: always inspect the entire frame on both sides before supporting the vehicle, as compromised areas can fail under load.
video-car-mechanics-101-yzuf1ytsxdm-yout.title: How to Check the Condition of Your Frame and Is It Safe to Work Under?

video-car-mechanics-101-zzwvijyqpdu-yout.summary: This video demonstrates a hands-on method to diagnose play in a front lower ball joint with a dial indicator. Andy explains how to distinguish load‑carrying from non‑load‑carrying joints by spring location, then shows unloading the suspension to take weight off the joint. Using locking pliers, a gauge, a floor jack, and a pry bar, the presenter zeroes the gauge, lifts the tire for a measured vertical movement, and compares the observed play to a 0.020 inch (20 thousandths) tolerance. A movement around 0.050 inches indicates replacement is needed, while smaller movements may be acceptable depending on tolerances from the repair manual. The example uses a 2009 Chevy Suburban and ends with guidance to consult the repair manual for vehicle-specific tolerances.
video-car-mechanics-101-zzwvijyqpdu-yout.title: How to Diagnose a Bad Ball Joint
